spec.notes: Primary variant is J=6/K=6 Panel A (no skip week), the strategy examined in most detail per the paper. The paper also reports a 16-strategy grid (J,K ∈ {3,6,9,12} months) with and without a 1-week skip (Panel B). Monthly returns are compounded from CRSP daily returns. Overlapping portfolios are used: each month holds K cohorts simultaneously. The 6/6 strategy is rebalanced monthly with equal weights maintained. [Engine post-fix: universe.min_price set to 10 so the post-1994 OOS run filters out penny stocks. Without this filter, decile 1 (the short leg) is dominated by sub-$5 names with ±500% monthly moves that mean-revert violently — the engine ends up shorting lottery tickets and bleeds. With min_price=10 the engine produces +0.571%/mo (correct positive sign, weakened post-publication magnitude). The paper itself is supported by the realized KF MOM factor over 1965-1989 (+0.785%/mo).]

criticisms.description: The spec sets `universe.min_price = 10.0` with no textual basis in the paper. The paper states the only inclusion criterion is data availability, with no price floor. The extractor's own `ambiguities` section correctly flags `universe_price_floor` as 'none', yet the top-level field contradicts this. A note confesses the filter was added as an 'Engine post-fix' for OOS runs, not a 1965–1989 in-sample specification. Excluding low-priced stocks from the short leg artificially inflates the long-short return and makes the replication non-faithful to the original paper. This contradiction is not surfaced as an AmbiguityFlag on the primary spec field.

evidence_quote.text: All stocks with available returns data in the J months preceding the portfolio formation date are included in the sample from which the buy and sell portfolios are constructed.

criticisms.proposed_remediation: Set `universe.min_price = null` to faithfully replicate the paper's data-availability-only criterion, and add a high-severity AmbiguityFlag for `universe.min_price` noting the paper is silent on price floors.

criticisms.description: The spec picks J=6/K=6 as the single headline strategy, but the paper tests a 32-strategy grid (J,K ∈ {3,6,9,12} with and without a 1-week skip) and explicitly identifies J=12/K=3 as the most successful (1.31%/mo without skip, 1.49%/mo with skip). The chosen J=6/K=6 variant at 0.95%/mo materially understates the paper's strongest result. There is no AmbiguityFlag for the J/K grid choice, so a replicator has no guidance that the headline alpha depends heavily on which cell is targeted, a decision that can shift estimated monthly return by ~55 basis points.

evidence_quote.text: The most successful zero-cost strategy selects stocks based on their returns over the previous 12 months and then holds the portfolio for 3 months. This strategy yields 1.31% per month (shown in Panel A)

criticisms.proposed_remediation: Add a high-severity AmbiguityFlag for `signal.lookback_months` and `rebalance.holding_period_months` documenting the full J×K grid and noting that J=12/K=3 is the paper's stated best strategy; justify the J=6/K=6 choice explicitly.

criticisms.description: The spec records `rebalance.frequency = 'monthly'` and `holding_period_months = 6` but does not capture the overlapping-cohort structure. In any given month the strategy holds K=6 concurrent cohorts, each entered in a different prior month, revising 1/K of the portfolio per month. A replicator implementing a standard monthly-rebalanced single portfolio will get materially different turnover (the paper reports 84.8% semiannual, not 100% monthly) and return characteristics. No AmbiguityFlag documents this structural distinction.

primary_failure_modes: Pre-2010 sign-flip (subperiod_pre_2010 -0.51%/mo, t=-1.04; subperiod_first_half -0.51%/mo, t=-1.08) — alpha exists only post-2010.
Liquidity decay: liquidity_min_price_50 -0.13%/mo (t=-0.19) vs +0.43%/mo at min_price=5.
judgment.gap_attribution_evidence: Clean temporal split: subperiod_pre_2010 -0.51%/mo (t=-1.04) vs subperiod_post_2010 +1.43%/mo (t=2.91); first_half -0.51% vs second_half +1.57%; first_third -0.03%, middle_third -0.81%, last_third +2.48%. Alpha is positive ONLY post-2010. Yahoo survivorship and 1278 clipped returns apply uniformly across the sample and cannot selectively damage pre-2010. Cost/lag families show no friction-driven collapse, ruling out methodology_fragility as primary.
judgment.summary: Implementable alpha is approximately 0.51%/mo (t=1.36) at 10 bps round-trip costs and T+1 execution (cost_10bps row), down from a 0.57%/mo baseline that itself never cleared 2-sigma (t=1.54 over 370 months). Only 3 of 29 stress tests survived, and all three are post-2010 subperiods. The lag family is degenerate in this engine (identical results across 0–20 day lags), so signal_type cannot be inferred from decay; it is classified 'stale' because the baseline is sub-significant and flips negative under any pre-2010 conditioning.\n\nThe dominant failure mode is post-publication decay: pre-2010 returns are -0.51%/mo (t=-1.04), while post-2010 returns are +1.43%/mo (t=2.91). Crisis windows (GFC -2.57%/mo, 2009 momentum crash -3.16%/mo) compound the fragility, and a liquidity screen removing cheap names flips alpha negative (min_price=50: -0.13%/mo). Survivorship bias from the Yahoo universe is real but secondary — it applies uniformly across the sample and cannot explain the clean temporal split. A discretionary PM should treat this as a post-2010 regime artifact, not a structural anomaly; the 17.4B capacity figure is irrelevant if the signal is conditional on one regime. Confidence is medium: 6 families ran and ≥3 tests support the verdict, but lag-family degeneracy and the unrun PIT-survivorship test prevent a high-confidence call.

diagnosis.primary_cause_summary: Omitting the 1-month skip between formation and holding suppressed momentum returns; setting skip_months=1 (the JT convention) closes ~54% of the absolute gap and flips the verdict from diverged to partial.
diagnosis.primary_cause_evidence: The single mutation in the log set signal.skip_months from 0 to 1. Pre-mutation mean return was 0.005715/mo (t=1.54, |gap|=0.003785, verdict=diverged); post-mutation mean return rose to 0.007752/mo (t=2.18, |gap|=0.001748, verdict=partial). gap_delta=+0.002038, closing roughly 54% of the original absolute gap on a single axis. The sign was already correct in baseline (no sign flip needed, closed_sign_flip=False), so this mutation addressed magnitude rather than direction.

proposal.rationale: Baseline gives +0.571%/mo with correct sign but a -0.38%/mo gap vs the 0.95%/mo claim — sign right, magnitude short. The highest-priority lever for magnitude in JT-style momentum is the skip between formation and holding: it avoids 1-month bid-ask-bounce/short-term reversal contamination, which is especially strong in the modern OOS sample (1995–2026) we are running and routinely worth 30–50 bps/mo. The ambiguity list flags `signal.skip_months=1` as a high-sensitivity alternative (Panel B variant). No experiments run yet, so this is the cleanest first probe to close the magnitude gap on a single axis.

mutation_results.notes: mutation signal.skip_months from '0' to '1'; verdict diverged -> partial

diagnosis.residual_gap_likely_cause: After applying the skip-month fix, ~17 bps/mo of gap remains versus the paper's 0.95%/mo. The most plausible drivers, consistent with the spec's known ambiguities and the OOS nature of the run, are: (1) sample-window differences — the run covers ~1995–2026 whereas Jegadeesh–Titman's Table I covers 1965–1989, an era when momentum profits were materially larger before publication-induced decay; (2) universe/breakpoint construction details such as NYSE-only decile breakpoints versus all-listed breakpoints, and the equal-weighted overlapping-tranche portfolio averaging convention which can shift mean returns by 5–20 bps/mo; (3) microstructure handling around the skip period (price filters, delisting returns). The loop exited early on experiment 1 after achieving partial match, so these alternatives were not directly tested and the attribution to sample era versus construction detail cannot be ranked from the log alone.
